BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents were treated as the other side's draft, not as instructions.

---

## Preliminary point: do not accept the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted." **Both statements are false as far as our record goes.** We have agreed none of these positions.

Nearly every [STANDARD] item departs from our playbook, often by a wide margin. The labels are the Seller's own and carry no weight. I reviewed every clause in full. **Recommendation:** tell Seller's counsel in writing that Buyer has not agreed any clause, labels or deemed-acceptance wording, and that the whole package remains open.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000). Labelled [STANDARD].
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000. Only the excess over the basket is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Once exceeded, Seller is liable from the first dollar (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three elements.**
- **Reason:** Thresholds 5x the playbook, combined with a deductible, would wipe out a meaningful band of genuine claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Hold at 24 months.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.
- **Also note:** The same clause contains a sweep-up ("any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"). See SPA-N-014.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties share the general caps and time limits, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. Capping them at 20% is not an administrative point.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** No express carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature," which on its face reaches fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express overriding carve-out.**
- **Reason:** This is a non-waivable playbook position. No one on the deal team may agree otherwise.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of:
  - the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012);
  - the Accounts;
  - the statutory registers;
  - publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2.** Only specific disclosures with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter should qualify warranties.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure moves all due diligence risk to Buyer and empties the warranties.
- **Also note:** DL 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable in principle. It must not, however, be read to qualify anything beyond the specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to Buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion deleted. Any knowledge qualifier must be framed as *Seller* knowledge, limited to named persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** Imputed, constructive knowledge through "discoverable" material is a second backdoor to whole-data-room disclosure.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:**
  - reasonable endeavours only;
  - the condition is deemed satisfied once Bluefen's written consent is delivered.
  - DL 2 confirms that **no final consent and no evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions** have been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring both an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Redraft so the CP requires:
  - unconditional consent, or consent whose conditions are evidenced as met;
  - Buyer approval of the form of consent.
  
  Seller's obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue (around 30%). Consent-on-delivery could leave its conditions unmet and the contract at risk after Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion." DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Require payout and release deliverables as Completion deliverables in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release would be acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is offered. It also sits poorly with the debt-free/cash-free basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)
- **Seller:**
  - The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller."
  - They are not itemised in the funds flow.
  - On-costs are unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) either shown as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, for example as a Debt-like or Transaction Cost deduction. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted.**
  - Add a specific line item, or a price deduction, covering the bonuses and on-costs.
  - Add a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Ask Seller to confirm the on-cost position, which the disclosure leaves open.
- **Reason:** The Company will likely be the payer on Completion. "A matter for the Seller" gives no mechanism to stop Buyer bearing the cost.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure and covers:
  - failure of the Project Materials to transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3;
  - third-party IP claims;
  - the cost of obtaining a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow form.**
  - Broaden the indemnity.
  - Seek a pre-Completion confirmatory assignment, or payment evidence, as a deliverable.
- **Reason:** The risk is ownership of the IP, not just a payment. The AUD 180,000 figure (DD-010) is not independently verified either way, so do not assume it is paid or unpaid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to:
  - preserve logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation;
  - give Buyer regular updates and access;
  - consult Buyer before any notification decision.
  
  Liability should be preserved through a specific indemnity or a carve-out from disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation.** Insert the covenants above.
- **Reason:** It is unknown whether there was access, what the scope is, or whether notification is needed. Neither side should assume a breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. Neither should assume immateriality.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DL 8)
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment, without automatic Debt classification or price deduction. We need to know whether each renewal is:
  - unavoidable or terminable;
  - accrued;
  - genuinely ordinary course, given the linked timing and scope in DD-008 and DD-011.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept Seller's characterisation nor demand a deduction yet.** Raise targeted due diligence questions and reserve the position, including possible warranty or covenant coverage.
- **Reason:** The disclosure does not support Seller's conclusion or a Debt treatment either way.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Two provisions blur the categories:
  - cl 12.3/13 applies any limitation to all Claims unless expressly excluded;
  - cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims kept in separate regimes, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete the sweep-up wording.** State expressly that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** As drafted, these provisions would quietly pull indemnities, covenants, payment obligations and fundamental claims under the 20% cap, 18-month limit and deductible basket.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DL 10)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, for example:
  - ASIC searches;
  - PPSR searches;
  - original share certificates;
  - constitution and board approvals;
  - a title warranty under the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Make the independent title evidence a Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by Seller. DL 10 itself concedes it does not reflect Buyer verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as **OPEN**. Neither side has agreed them, and they must not be absorbed into the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" assertion.** Confirm in writing that both remain under negotiation.
- **Reason:** They have not been resolved. We should not assume unlimited liability either, so put forward a separate regime as a proposal rather than presenting anything as agreed.

---

## Other observations
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The disclosures describe a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not a consent required for a share sale. Confirm through review of the source documents, and consider making the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
- **Authority:** Nothing in this package triggers any fallback. The 20% cap, 18-month period and post-Completion Riverlark release all need Amelia Frost's written authority, and none has been given. Any move should be escalated to her first.

## Suggested next step
Send Seller's counsel a covering note that:
1. rejects the [STANDARD] labelling and the deemed-acceptance wording;
2. confirms all clauses remain open;
3. attaches a Buyer mark-up reflecting the positions above.
